judge_panel.matching_evidence:
[numerical] The null-geodesic function \(F(\gamma)\) has an inconsistent numerical coefficient, Sec. 3, Eqs. (61) and (65).

Eq. (61) gives
\[
\int \Theta\,d\alpha = \frac{3}{\gamma}.
\tag{61}
\]
But the theorem then states that for a null geodesic
\[
F(\gamma)=\frac{2}{\gamma}.
\tag{65}
\]
These cannot both be correct under the definitions printed in the paper.

Concrete fix: replace Eq. (65) by the coefficient implied by the corrected derivation. If Eq. (61) remains as printed after the sign convention is fixed, Eq. (65) should read \(F(\gamma)=3/\gamma\).
judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer explicitly identifies the exact inconsistent value 2/gamma versus 3/gamma in the theorem statement, which is the injected numeric change.

judge_panel.matching_evidence:
[mathematical] The Lorentz factor is misstated, Sec. 1, Eq. (10).

Eq. (10) prints
\[
\gamma^2=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-v^2}}.
\tag{10}
\]
The standard relation is
\[
\gamma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-v^2}},
\qquad
\gamma^2=\frac{1}{1-v^2}.
\]
The surrounding derivation uses \(\gamma^2\) as \((dt/ds)^2\), so the printed Eq. (10) is inconsistent with the standard definition.

Concrete fix: replace Eq. (10) with either \(\gamma=1/\sqrt{1-v^2}\) or \(\gamma^2=1/(1-v^2)\).
judge_panel.reasoning: This exactly matches the injected algebraic identity replacement, quoting the incorrect printed formula and the correct one.
